messages:
lina: Heads-up: updated modal mock for the encryption & region step in the data lifecycle flow. Looking for quick UX + compliance nits before I hand off to eng.

dan: Saw the mock. Two quick surface items: the modal lists three options in this order: "Redwood KMS", "Bring your own key (BYOK)", "No encryption". Is "No encryption" allowed for orgs with compliance lock? Might need to hide it behind a gate.

mei: Good catch. Policy-wise we should hide "No encryption" for orgs with `security.enforce_encryption=true`. If we show a disabled state, the tooltip must explain why it's disabled: "Disabled by org policy: encryption required".

sam: Accessibility: the region menu is visually a select with flags. Screen reader sees it as a plain button. Use <select role="listbox"> semantics or ensure aria-label includes the country name. Also the flag alone is not sufficient.

lina: Copy question: current inline copy says "Keys: Redwood-managed or BYOK" — too terse. Proposal: "Key management: Redwood-managed (recommended) / Customer-managed (BYOK)" and a short microcopy underneath for exportability.

dan: On exportability language, I prefer explicit verbs. Eg: "Cannot export key material." vs "No export." Prefer the first. Also, call out retention interplay: "Note: Changing key or region may re-encrypt recent data."

mei: Audit & telemetry: any change must emit both a human-readable audit event and a machine event. Suggest event id `security.kms.selection.v1` and a human message template: "{user} selected {kms_type} for org {org}, previous: {old_kms}". Include ip and request id.

sam: Keyboard order suggestion: 1) radio group for KMS choice, 2) inline explainer toggle (collapsed by default), 3) region picker, 4) secondary link "Why this matters" that opens a doc in a new tab, 5) primary Save. Escape should close only if no unsaved changes, otherwise prompt.

lina: UX heatmap note: in mock the BYOK option has a tiny badge "BYOK" next to it, but users didn't notice. Maybe replace badge with a subtle chip that says "Requires KMS admin" and an info icon. Also ensure color contrast meets AA.

dan: Dev constraints: if we show chip + icon, it's an extra node in the DOM. For performance we should reuse the existing Badge component and avoid adding JS-heavy tooltips. Use CSS-only tooltip with accessible fallback text.

mei: Legal wants the wording around export to avoid promising ability to "export key material" in the UI unless the customer can actually do it in-code. Suggest: "Subject to your KMS policy, customers may export key material." (ugh). Maybe add a link to the KMS capability doc.

lina: ok i'll draft a short set of copy strings for the modal:
```
Header: Encryption & processing region
KMS option 1: Redwood-managed (recommended)
KMS option 1 subtext: Redwood stores and rotates keys for you. Key material cannot be exported.
KMS option 2: Customer-managed (BYOK)
KMS option 2 subtext: Use your KMS. Export and rotation depend on your KMS policy. Requires KMS admin privileges.
Region label: Processing region (default: United States)
Region hint: Some integrations or features may vary by region.
```

sam: That looks good. For screen readers: expanders must set aria-expanded and aria-controls. Also when the info link opens a doc in a new tab it should include rel="noopener noreferrer" and an aria-label like "Opens in new tab".

dan: Audit naming final proposal: human event title = "KMS selection changed"; machine id = `audit.kms.change.v1`. We should also keep an alias `audit.kms.choice` for legacy listeners for 90 days.

infra-bot: note: component tokens updated in branch `design/kms-modal` at 1876599901. CI lint passed.

lina: Great. Action items: (1) I'll update the figma copy + add the KMS admin chip, (2) @mei will draft the audit event payload and alias plan, (3) @sam will add keyboard sequence notes to the PR, (4) @dan will confirm disabled-state behavior for org policies. Will follow up when PR is ready for review.
